summary: Finland is permissive for the roof rat. There is no species-specific ban: R. rattus is not on the EU invasive-species Union list (Reg. 1143/2014) and not on Finland's national invasive list (Government Decree 1725/2015, updated 2023 — which covers alien carnivores, bats and chipmunks, not rats). The Animal Welfare Act (Eläinten hyvinvointilaki 693/2023, in force 2024) sets welfare/husbandry standards for all kept animals but doesn't restrict keeping R. rattus, so a hobbyist is in the same position as a fancy-rat (R. norvegicus) keeper. A notification to the Regional State Administrative Agency (AVI) is needed only at scale — reported as 7+ cages for professional activity, or 20+ cages for large-scale non-professional keeping. Intra-EU non-commercial movement of pet rodents needs no health certificate; commercial movement uses TRACES.

keep.why: R. rattus is absent from the EU Union list and Finland's national invasive list (Decree 1725/2015, updated 2023). The Animal Welfare Act 693/2023 applies welfare/housing standards to all kept animals but lists no prohibited pet rodent. No Finnish dangerous-exotic decree names roof rats. Medium (not high) confidence only because no Finnish authority has published an explicit 'R. rattus permitted' statement — a one-line confirmation from Ruokavirasto would settle it.
keep.governing_law: Laki eläinten hyvinvoinnista 693/2023; Government Decree 1725/2015 (R. rattus not listed); Reg. (EU) 1143/2014 (not listed).

breed.why: Hobby breeding is not prohibited, but the Animal Welfare Act 693/2023 requires a NOTIFICATION to AVI for professional or large-scale keeping: reported thresholds are ~7 cages/terraria/aquaria (professional/commercial) or ~20 (large-scale non-professional), filed at least 30 days before starting. Below those, no registration. A dedicated rattery can approach the 20-cage line, so flag it — but it's a notification, not a hard licence.
breed.governing_law: Laki eläinten hyvinvoinnista 693/2023 (notification-required activities); AVI guidance.

sell_give.why: No prohibition on selling/giving captive-bred R. rattus. Selling or regularly transferring as part of a professional or large-scale operation triggers the same AVI notification (7-cage professional threshold; all premises of a large-scale operation registered). Free transfers between hobbyists below threshold are unregulated. Commercial sale → register with AVI + welfare inspection.
sell_give.governing_law: Laki eläinten hyvinvoinnista 693/2023; AVI / Ruokavirasto guidance.

transport.why: Internal transport: no species restriction, only fitness-for-transport welfare rules. Intra-EU non-commercial movement by an owner accompanying the animals needs no import permit and no health certificate (Ruokavirasto guidance for rodents); customs may inspect. Commercial intra-EU trade uses TRACES + the rodent health-certificate model. Caveat: the import ban applies to species ON the EU/national invasive list — R. rattus is on neither, so it doesn't apply. Never release.
transport.governing_law: Ruokavirasto import/movement guidance; EU Reg. 2016/429; Laki eläinten hyvinvoinnista 693/2023.

restrictions.summary: Breeding/selling rats professionally (~7 cages) or large-scale (~20 cages) requires a NOTIFICATION to your Regional State Administrative Agency (AVI) at least 30 days before you start. Below that, hobby keeping/breeding/rehoming is unregistered — just meet the welfare standards. Never release a roof rat.
steps: If at/above the cage threshold, file an AVI notification (Suomi.fi portal) 30 days before commencing

inquiry_focus: (1) Is Rattus rattus (mustarotta/kattorotta) subject to any restriction under Finland's national invasive alien species decree (1725/2015, updated Aug 2023) or Finland's implementation of EU Reg. 1143/2014 that would restrict keeping it as a pet — i.e., is it on the national list or not? (2) Under the Animal Welfare Act 693/2023, what is the exact notification threshold for a private individual breeding small hobby rodents such as rats — does the 7-cage or 20-cage threshold apply, and is anything beyond notification required? (3) For non-commercial movement of captive-bred R. rattus from another EU member state by the owner personally, are there any species-specific documentation/health-certificate requirements?

sources.title: Laki eläinten hyvinvoinnista 693/2023 — Animal Welfare Act (no prohibited pet-rodent list; AVI notification at scale)
Government Decree 1725/2015 on invasive alien species of national concern (carnivores/bats/chipmunks; R. rattus absent)
AVI — Notifications for professional or large-scale keeping of animals (cage thresholds)
Ruokavirasto — Rabbits and rodents, intra-EU movement (no health cert for non-commercial)
Regulation (EU) 1143/2014 on invasive alien species — Union list (R. rattus not listed)
Regulation (EU) 2016/429 — Animal Health Law (intra-EU movement framework)
